card.name: Words before a reported statistical result
card.fires_on: Small words like a, an, was or statistically right before a clinical-trial result is stated, such as a significant or non-significant increase or reduction in risk.

modes.label: Article before result
modes.description: The word a or an comes just before a significant or non-significant finding.

modes.label: Was before comparison
modes.description: The verb was follows a trial outcome like survival and precedes a comparison wording.
modes.example: Overall survival<< was>> significantly shorter in patients receiving epoet

modes.label: Statistical qualifier
modes.description: The word statistically or part of significant comes before a described risk change.
modes.example: a<< statistically>> significant increased risk of stroke was reported in

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words like trend and trends, as in a trend toward higher or lower risk.
card.plain: It fires on the little words just before a trial result is described, where the text may say a trend or a significant change.
